prompt: Design an implementation-ready accessibility system for a controller-first action game, using the six game task IDs and five information channels from the supplied scope corpus. Current scenarios: remapping the Confirm button conflicts with Back and Pause; a controller disconnects during a timed boss attack; an urgent directional, non-speech alarm is conveyed only by audio; the boss shows a brief red-only attack telegraph; health, stamina, and ammunition change quickly; camera shake and automatic tracking cause motion sensitivity; a 40-item upgrade tree is dense; and online co-op uses voice-only instructions and cannot pause the whole session. Define reachable input and recovery behavior (including reconnect and saved bindings), captions/descriptions that convey source and urgency, redundant spatial and status cues, visual clarity and optional timing adjustments, motion/camera controls, screen narration, readable menu/HUD and upgrade navigation, text or ping alternatives to voice, and an online-safe pause/settings path with stated gameplay tradeoffs. Specify accessible task outcomes, negative states, fail/recovery invariants, component ownership, and priority for each. Produce .kory-eval/game-accessibility.json and a verification matrix spanning game platform/build, controller and alternative input, accessibility settings, representative tutorial/combat/co-op/menu/recovery state, expected observable behavior, method, status, result/evidence reference, and remaining risk. The synthetic fixture provides no console/PC game runtime, controller hardware, or assistive-technology session: record unexecuted rows as planned/untested; never invent passed tests. Use game/platform guidance as best practice rather than a universal compliance verdict; do not import web markup/CSS mechanics. Baseline/candidate comparisons and blind judgment require independent execution, which is not supplied by this design task.

requirements: fixed task/channel scope corpus and synthetic README from registered materializer
controller remap collisions, disconnection mid-combat, sensory-only cues, and upgrade-menu orientation
offline and online pause constraints must be distinguished; actual platform and game build are unknown
no real game runtime, controller, accessibility settings capture, or co-op session is provided
paired same-model comparison requires independently recorded baseline and candidate artifacts

falsifiableChecks.assertion: All six scope-corpus game task IDs have success, failure, and recovery routes; remapping a reserved Confirm/Back/Pause binding reports a conflict, keeps essential actions reachable by an alternative input method, offers a recoverable choice/default, and persists or rolls back safely when a controller disconnects during combat.

All five fixed information channels have independently usable alternatives. A directional non-speech alarm conveys source/direction and urgency without audio; a short red-only attack telegraph has a persistent or adjustable, non-color channel; health/stamina/ammunition changes and co-op instructions remain comprehensible without a single sensory channel or voice chat.

Camera shake/tracking controls, optional cue durations or safe alternatives, legible/scale-aware HUD, independent health/stamina/ammo status, screen narration, and a keyboard/controller/alternative-input path through a 40-item upgrade tree specify focus/selection, purchase/undo, and return-to-context behavior without erasing core gameplay objectives.

A matrix covers menu, tutorial, combat, co-op communication, pause/settings, and recovery with device/build identity if known, input/AT/configuration, exact triggered state, expected observable result, method, execution status, observed result or null, provenance and residual risk. Distinguish solo/offline pause from online shared-time constraints, and mark absent runtime/hardware untested.

Requirements use relevant platform/game guidance as best practice, separate assumptions from known game constraints, avoid HTML/DOM/CSS navigation mechanics, and never infer conformance or spoken game narration from a static or synthetic plan.

Regression probes give a reproducible trigger, failure observation and recovery invariant for remap collisions that strand Back, disconnect/reconnect during an attack, directionless audio-only alarms, missed short color-only telegraphs, upgrade selection lost on pagination, online Pause falsely freezing shared play, and voice-only co-op decisions.

evidence: all six fixed tasks and five information channels have equivalent objectives
conflicting remaps and controller disconnect/reconnect recovery
dialogue captions, directional non-speech alternatives and non-color combat cues
motion/camera, cue timing, HUD and upgrade-tree access
voice-independent co-op communication and online pause limitations
negative-path/regression oracles tied to observable game state
six-task gameplay, menu and recovery matrix, including online and offline constraints
methods, status, observed result, evidence provenance and risk
synthetic design cannot attest real controller or narration results
XAG-style best practices without browser mechanics or invented conformance
